mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Velar P400 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A reconditioned or rebuilt Range Rover Velar P400 engine typically costs between £6,500 and £13,000 for the supply-only unit, depending on the level of rebuild and specialist documentation provided.
- Rebuilt units include upgraded cooling components and supercharger coupler checks.
- Supply and fit packages are available through our premium specialist network.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of supercharger or cooling failure in a Range Rover Velar P400?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Early detection is critical to preventing catastrophic damage to your Range Rover Velar P400 engine.
- Look for unexplained coolant loss, sudden overheating warnings, or a distinct rattling noise from the supercharger at idle.
- Sweet-smelling exhaust smoke or oil contamination are also strong indicators of internal failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a high-value Range Rover Velar P400?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, given the strong retained values of the Velar P400, replacing the engine is a highly sound financial decision.
- A typical 2019-2024 model is valued between £25,000 and £45,000+, making a £7,500-£13,000 rebuild a small percentage of the vehicle's worth.
- A rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty adds reliability and protects your premium asset.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Velar P400 engine supply and fit take?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A straightforward supply and fit replacement for a Range Rover Velar P400 typically takes 4 to 6 days at a premium specialist workshop.
- This allows time for the engine to be delivered, mounted, and thoroughly calibrated and tested.
- Complex cases requiring additional cooling system or supercharger upgrades may take slightly longer.

mainEntity.name: Can I upgrade my Range Rover Velar to a P400 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text:
While the Velar chassis was designed with multiple powertrain options, a retrofit is not straightforward.
- The P400 3.0L supercharged engine requires extensive ECU mapping, bespoke wiring harnesses, and upgraded cooling systems to function correctly and pass MOT.
- We strongly recommend sticking to a like-for-like replacement to ensure guaranteed compatibility, reliability, and warranty coverage.

historyTimeline.intro: The P400 badge on the Range Rover Velar represents the pinnacle of the supercharged V6 era, offering a seamless blend of 400hp performance and refined luxury before the model line consolidated around four-cylinder Ingenium and PHEV powertrains.

milestones.description: AJ126 / AJ133 (2995cc), 400hp, launched as the top-tier petrol option for the Velar, featuring a twin-scroll turbocharger and electric supercharger for instant throttle response and refined power delivery.

2024 - Continued availability in high-spec trims (e.g., HSE, First Edition) before the range shifted focus towards the P400e PHEV and D300/D350 mild-hybrid variants, cementing the P400 as a highly sought-after performance variant.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover Velar P400 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Range Rover Velar P400 features a robust 3.0-litre supercharged V6 engine. While generally more reliable than the diesel Ingenium variants, the forced-induction system and complex cooling architecture require specialist attention. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Supercharger Coupler Wear & Coolant Leaks - Why the Range Rover Velar P400 AJ126 / AJ133 Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: The supercharger isolator coupler degrades over time, causing a distinct rattling noise at idle. Additionally, plastic coolant crossover pipes can become brittle and leak under high under-bonnet temperatures, risking overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace supercharger coupler and plastic coolant pipes with revised aluminium parts.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended preventative maintenance to avoid catastrophic overheating or supercharger damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if neglect has led to severe overheating, warped heads, or deep mechanical knocking.

problems.recommendation: If your Velar P400 exhibits early supercharger rattle or minor coolant leaks, preventative specialist repair is highly cost-effective. However, if the engine has suffered overheating damage, HPFP failure leading to internal damage, or severe timing chain stretch, a full reconditioned replacement is the most reliable long-term solution.

problems.group: High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) & Timing Chain Wear
problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) & Timing Chain Wear - Why the Range Rover Velar P400 AJ126 / AJ133 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The HPFP can fail, leading to hard starting or misfires. Timing chain tensioners can also wear under high-stress performance driving, causing a cold-start rattle that risks chain skip.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace HPFP and inspect/replace timing chain components with revised JLR specification parts.
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught early before chain skip causes valve-to-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain failure has already caused internal valvetrain or piston damage.
